chats.answer:
You need a USB-C cable rated for both 240W USB Power Delivery (PD 3.1 EPR) and 40Gbps data transfer.

These two specifications are independent, so not every 240W cable supports 40Gbps, and not every 40Gbps cable supports 240W.

Look for these specifications:

Feature

	

Required specification




Charging

	

240W (48V × 5A), USB PD 3.1 EPR




Data transfer

	

40Gbps




Connector

	

USB-C to USB-C




Cable type

	

USB4 40Gbps or Thunderbolt 4 with explicit 240W support




Simultaneous use

	

Yes, charging and data can operate together

A cable supporting both can charge your laptop while transferring data through a compatible dock or external SSD, although actual charging power and transfer speed depend on the connected devices.

One important distinction: A cable rated for 240W doesn't guarantee 240W charging. Your charger, device, and any intervening dock must support the necessary USB PD power levels. Similarly, 40Gbps is the maximum link rate, not guaranteed file-transfer throughput.

What are you connecting? For example, a laptop to a Thunderbolt dock, or a laptop directly to an external SSD? That determines whether you can actually get both capabilities simultaneously.
